mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for at least 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a contraction in the housing sector amid monetary tightening, which triggers a negative earnings outlook and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where HOUST declines and FEDFUNDS rises simultaneously, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity that reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows in late-cycle expansions is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past three months indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS has increased for at least 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall by more than 5% over a three-month period, it signals a contraction in the residential sector that reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST falls by more than 5% over three months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces household income and consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises simultaneously, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs that depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows in tightening cycles is below 0.03.
